input: Find bribery and corruption enforcement involving Ericsson, including its deferred prosecution agreement

entity.group: Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson (publ) — standalone listed parent group (Nasdaq Stockholm; NASDAQ New York), registration number 556016-0680

events.date: SEC investigation began 2013; DOJ investigation began 2015; publicly disclosed June 17, 2016
events.summary: Multi-year US criminal and civil investigation into Ericsson's anticorruption program and FCPA violations; Ericsson accrued SEK 12 billion (~$1 billion) in September 2019 in anticipation of the resolution.

events.amount: $520,650,432 total criminal penalty (a 15% reduction off the bottom of the Sentencing Guidelines range; part of a >$1 billion global resolution with the SEC)
events.parties: Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson with the DOJ Criminal Division Fraud Section and U.S. Attorney's Office for the SDNY (United States v. Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson, 19-CR-00884-AJN, S.D.N.Y.)
events.summary: Ericsson entered a three-year DPA over a two-count criminal information charging conspiracies to violate the FCPA anti-bribery, books-and-records and internal controls provisions for 2000–2016 conduct — bribes via third-party agents/consultants, sham contracts and false invoices in Djibouti, China, Vietnam, Indonesia and Kuwait — with a three-year independent compliance monitor and cooperation obligations.
events.jurisdiction: United States (S.D.N.Y.; DOJ Criminal Division Fraud Section)

events.summary: Ericsson's Egyptian subsidiary pleaded guilty in the Southern District of New York to a one-count criminal information charging conspiracy to violate the FCPA anti-bribery provisions.

events.amount: More than $539 million in disgorgement and prejudgment interest
events.summary: SEC charged Ericsson with a large-scale bribery scheme using sham consultants to funnel money to government officials: conduct 2011–2017 in Saudi Arabia and Djibouti (business valued at ~$427 million obtained via third-party bribes) and further violations in Vietnam, Indonesia and Kuwait (slush funds, code names, sham transactions and invoices).

events.type: Follow-on civil settlement (claim arising from the 2019 FCPA resolution)
events.summary: Ericsson settled competitor Nokia's claim for 'uncertainty, risk, and expense from the prolonged and complex litigation' relating to the events underlying the 2019 DOJ/SEC FCPA resolutions; €80 million hit Ericsson's Q2 2021 EBIT.
DOJ determined Ericsson breached its 2019 DPA obligations by failing to provide certain documents and factual information.

events.amount: Tens of millions of dollars in suspicious payments from 2011–2019
events.summary: ICIJ and ~30 media partners reported that Ericsson allegedly paid tens of millions of dollars in suspicious payments 2011–2019, sought permission from Islamic State (ISIS) to work in an ISIS-controlled city, and paid to smuggle equipment into ISIS areas via the 'Speedway' route; Ericsson said its internal investigation found compliance violations but no evidence of payments to terrorist organizations.

events.type: DPA breach finding (failure to disclose Iraq investigation)
events.summary: DOJ informed Ericsson its pre-DPA disclosure about its internal investigation into conduct in Iraq (2011–2019 — corruption-related misconduct, internal-control violations, conflicts of interest, obstruction, and alternate transport routes circumventing Iraqi Customs, some controlled by ISIS) was insufficient and that it breached the DPA by failing to make subsequent disclosures.
The SEC notified Ericsson it had initiated an investigation into the Iraq misconduct.

events.amount: Nearly $20 million 3G contract at issue; prosecutors alleged nearly $2 million in bribes
events.parties: Four former Ericsson executives (prosecuted by Swedish prosecutors; prosecutor Mats Jansson)
events.summary: Solna District Court acquitted four former Ericsson executives of bribing high-ranking Djibouti officials to win a 3G contract worth nearly $20 million, ruling prosecutors did not prove the money was received; the prosecutor said he would review the verdict for appeal. One of the four is separately being prosecuted in the US, charged with arranging more than $2 million in bribes to three officials to beat out Huawei for a contract in Djibouti.

events.parties: Families of slain and injured plaintiffs v. Ericsson
events.summary: Families of slain and injured plaintiffs sued Ericsson over claims it funded Middle East terror (reported by ICIJ).

events.date: December 14, 2022 (Ericsson press release; ICIJ reported December 15, 2022)
events.status: settled (monitorship extended one year, to June 2024)
events.summary: Ericsson agreed to a one-year extension of the independent corporate compliance monitorship imposed in the 2019 settlement, following the DPA breaches.

events.type: Criminal enforcement — guilty plea following breach of the 2019 DPA
events.amount: $206,728,848 additional criminal penalty (includes elimination of the cooperation credit originally awarded under the 2019 DPA)
events.parties: Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson (DOJ Criminal Division Fraud Section; U.S. Attorney's Office SDNY; AAG Kenneth A. Polite Jr.; U.S. Attorney Damian Williams)
events.summary: After breaching the 2019 DPA's cooperation and disclosure provisions — failing to truthfully disclose all factual information and evidence about the Djibouti and China schemes and failing to promptly disclose evidence and allegations about its Iraq business — Ericsson agreed to plead guilty to two counts (conspiracy to violate the FCPA anti-bribery provisions and conspiracy to violate the books-and-records and internal controls provisions), pay an additional criminal penalty of $206,728,848, serve probation through June 2024, and extend the independent compliance monitor by one year.

events.type: SEC whistleblower award linked to the Ericsson bribery case
events.amount: $279 million — a record, topping the previous $114 million record (October 2020)
events.parties: SEC and an anonymous whistleblower (two other claimants denied)
events.summary: The SEC issued a record-breaking $279 million whistleblower award to an anonymous tipster whose information was crucial to the Ericsson investigation, under SEC rules paying 10–30% of fines collected.

events.date: March 28, 2024 (monitor certification); June 2, 2024 (monitorship and plea agreement concluded; announced June 3, 2024)
events.type: Conclusion of compliance monitorship and plea agreement
events.parties: Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson / DOJ independent compliance monitor
events.summary: The independent monitor certified to DOJ on March 28, 2024 that Ericsson's anti-corruption compliance program satisfied requirements and was functioning effectively; the monitorship (appointed June 2020) and the 2023 plea agreement expired June 2, 2024, and Ericsson said it continues to cooperate fully with DOJ and SEC investigations on historical conduct.

events.status: closed (SEC stated it did not intend to bring an enforcement action)
events.summary: The SEC informed Ericsson on September 26, 2024 that it closed its investigation into the Iraq misconduct and did not intend to bring an enforcement action.

events.date: Ongoing as of the most recent available reporting (Stanford FCPA dataset updated July 30, 2025; no 2025–2026 closure found)
events.summary: The DOJ investigation of Ericsson's conduct in Iraq and possible bribery payments remains open; Ericsson states it is cooperating. The 2023 plea agreement covered only the DPA breach, not the Iraq conduct.

output.assessment: Ericsson (Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson, Stockholm) is a proven repeat FCPA offender with an aggravating enforcement history: it resolved a 16-year, five-country bribery scheme in December 2019 for over $1 billion (a $520.65 million DOJ criminal penalty under a deferred prosecution agreement plus >$539 million to the SEC), then breached that DPA twice (2021 and 2022, including over Iraq/Islamic State-related disclosures), forcing it to plead guilty in March 2023 and pay a further $206.7 million — bringing total US criminal and civil payments above $1.2 billion, plus an €80 million follow-on settlement with Nokia and a record $279 million SEC whistleblower award tied to the case. Mitigating the near-term picture, the independent monitor certified the compliance program in March 2024 and the monitorship and plea agreement ended June 2, 2024, and the SEC closed its Iraq probe in September 2024 without action. The principal open risks are the DOJ's still-unresolved Iraq investigation (ongoing as of the most recent available reporting, July 2025) and pending civil litigation by families alleging the group funded Middle East terror.
missing_fields: jurisdiction and case details of the August 2022 civil suit by families alleging Middle East terror funding (not stated on the page that reports it)
exact announcement date of the SEC $279 million whistleblower award (page carries the award details but only an article date of September 15, 2023)
any Ericsson bribery/corruption enforcement developments after July 30, 2025 (most recent retrieved source covering the DOJ Iraq probe is updated to that date; no 2025-2026 resolution found)

excluded_namesakes.name: The Goldman Sachs Group, Inc.
excluded_namesakes.reason: A DOJ 'Deferred Prosecution Agreement' document surfaced while locating Ericsson's DPA, but it belongs to the Goldman Sachs 1MDB FCPA case (Cr. No. 20-437, E.D.N.Y.) — a different company entirely; excluded.

excluded_namesakes.name: LM Ericsson Telephone Company
excluded_namesakes.reason: Not a namesake: this is the alias used for the same legal entity (Telefonaktiebolaget LM Ericsson) in the Stanford FCPA investigations dataset; included in events rather than excluded.
